method.label: A right angle from the circle

annotationRationale: Cyclic opposite angles produce the right angle at M. Cosine-law expressions and two Pythagorean equations force x+y=3; triangle area and the quadratic formula finish the length calculation.
sourceMethod: Followed the first official solution, using cyclicity, the law of cosines, and Pythagorean equations. Made the equality IM=ME explicit to simplify the official product equation.

review.mathCheck: Cyclicity makes \(IME\) right. Independent cosine-law and Pythagorean calculations give \(x+y=3\) and \(IM^2=ME^2=x^2-3x+9/2\). Area 2 forces this square length to equal 4, so \(x=(3\pm\sqrt7)/2\). The condition \(x<y\) selects \(CI=(3-\sqrt7)/2\), yielding 12, choice D.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, originally worded adaptation of official solution 20's first approach on pages 10–11. Recognizing equal legs before using the area replaces the source's squared-product calculation without changing its method. The construction agrees with the supplied figure.
review.annotationCheck: Cyclic angles, cosine-law application, and Pythagorean relations are appropriately assessed. Triangle area and the quadratic formula correctly serve as support; root selection is explained.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: The exact cyclic-quadrilateral, Pythagorean, triangle-area, and quadratic-formula links match their uses. The general cosine-law node has no supplied CN alignment; its valid competition role does not require a substitute.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: G-C.A.3 supplies partial cyclic-angle coverage; G-SRT.D.10/11 supply partial cosine-law coverage. The solution applies these properties at 45 degrees without constructions, proofs, or sine-law generality. It demonstrates planar Pythagorean lengths, triangle-area calculation, and quadratic-formula use under 8.G.B.7, 6.G.A.1, and A-REI.B.4/4b; it does not demonstrate decomposition or the B.4a formula derivation.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: All five direct nodes fit the actual argument. The cosine-law node accommodates the included 45-degree angles, and the assessed geometry establishes the key relation before background area and quadratic calculations finish the solution.
